lines: Question chat: a few invited accounts see an Ask button that answers questions about the sim and their character (it can run the sim and read the game data). Nobody else sees anything. The privacy page has a section on what it sends.

Conversion: a skill's own conversion (Lightning Arrow, Hoarfrost Volley, Fuse Arrow and the other elemental attacks) now takes every damage type, not only Physical, and shares its 100% with conversion supports and gear, as in the game (Lightning Arrow + Ice leaves no Physical or Fire). Fuse Arrow and Lightning Arrow builds with conversion supports lose some damage in the sim.
Physical converted by a support (Ice, Flame, Zap) now gains the new element's more lines, such as Elemental Focus (game check: x1.547 on Hoarfrost Volley).
Skill tooltips and the Skill Scaling cards show each skill's conversion, and the tooltip lists what your supports, gear and Heralds add. The Damage tab's breakdown shows the conversion step.
Skill tooltips: gear and tree levels give attacks x1.03 each (the old text said about 1% past 5).
Chill: increased chill effect now raises chill up to 50% (it stopped at 30% before), as the game's Chill tooltip says. At 50% chill the enemy takes 35% more damage from hits.

Chill and Brittle no longer raise poison, ignite and bleed ticks (the game's text: ticks do not take them). Builds whose ticks were boosted by chill lose a little damage in the sim. Shock, chill and Brittle still add together.

Idol and Riven lines: the item window, the Build tab and gear tooltips now show these lines as the game does (the game scales some of them, for example idol Ballista and Totem speed x1.3: a 13 reads 17%), with the tier ranges to match. Damage numbers are unchanged; they already counted it.

Shock: the smallest shock now shrinks with how much of the hit is Lightning, as game tests showed. A skill that Ice leaves 40% Lightning shocks a big enemy for about 2.8% (before Shock Effect), not 7%. Lightning skills with Ice or another conversion lose a little damage in the sim; pure Lightning skills are unchanged.
FAQ: the Shock row explains this.
Crack: Damage over Time Multiplier and Freeze Duration now multiply each other on Crack (they used to add), as game tests on the Training Post showed. Cold builds with both deal a few percent more.
FAQ: new Crack section under Ailments, with the test numbers.
Trap with Spell Totem or Arrow Totem: the totem now always places the skill and Trap only adds its damage, whatever order they are socketed in. Before, Trap socketed first was simmed as thrown traps.
Market: Copy search on a listing copies its name to paste into the game's Market ("Name or base" box).
Market: Copy mods on a rare or magic listing copies its three best mods for the game's "Mods" box, so you can find that exact item there.
Market: the "top tier" mark shows from 2 best-tier mods, as in the game.
Market: Live search. Turn it on and the page checks the market every 5 minutes and alerts you when a new listing matches your filters (keep the page open).
Market: find Truesworn bases (Base Grade 90+) with a new mark, a Base Grade filter and a Base Grade sort.
Market: the Riven line mark and filter now say "Riven line (T0)", for searching Tier 0 lines.

New Market tab: search every item listed on the Wagon Market in the public trade leagues, by name, slot, mods, price, weapon and armour numbers and more. You still buy in the game, at the Settler Wagon.
Market: the Upgrade finder sims each listing on your character and shows what it does to your main skill's damage, with sorts for the biggest gain and the most gain for the price.
Market: every search has its own link to share, and listings show the game's marks (Signature, Pinnacle, Riven line, top tier mods).
Rain support: enemies are struck 3 times per use (4 with 4 or more projectiles), and a Ballista's bolts twice, as the support text and the game's skill panel say (the sim used 2 and 3).
Heralds: a hit's extra damage from one Herald is counted once. Damage converted by Ice (or another conversion) used to get it twice.
Hoarfrost Volley: a Ranger can use it at most once every 0.35 s, as the game shows; speed past that turns into damage, as for Split Shot.
Dragonling tree: node names and texts now show in every page language, using the game's own translations.
Dragonling tree: the panel's own labels and hints are translated too. The one-crown-at-a-time rule is confirmed by the game's own text.
FAQ, Damage Multipliers: the developer's stacking table (build 86) now lists the damage engine lines as adding, as the game does.
Dragonling tree: nodes that follow your Aspect show that Aspect's own text, as in the game (Cold Dragon's Heart: Hoarfrost Dive). Crowns show their 3-point cost.
Dragonling tree: the Dragon Ruptures box now shows the points you have earned, and the tree says when your picks cost more than that (not a valid tree in the game).
Recent Patch has a new TLDR view: one patch in plain English (new things, skills that got stronger or weaker, the numbers that moved).
Skill tree tab: the Dragonling panel has a search box. Matching nodes get a red ring and the rest dim.
Dragonling trees now match the game: 43 nodes the game does not have are gone (4 to 10 per class, e.g. Deep Chill and Ink of Stars for Mage). Builds that held one of them lose it, as in the game.
Damage numbers now follow only the game's own data and the current patch notes. Corrections taken from older patch notes are gone:
Piercing Shot, Gravereap, Ballista, Crescent Slash and Rain of Arrows lose an extra late-gem boost the sim added from the patch 79 notes (3 to 21% less).
Pyre of Faith and Unholy Void pulses now set off your on-hit effects again (an old patch 83 note said they did not).
Thunderfall no longer takes your spell damage lines (its current text does not say it does).
New icons for the Gravefeast gem and the Gravesown and Kindled Remains supports. Sworn Surge (was Elemental Overload) shows its new name in damage notes.
